site.title: Wilmington University Corner
site.description: A law school study library: outlines, rule charts, flowcharts, flashcards, and practice question banks you can open in the browser or download.

subjects.title: Evidence
subjects.description: Federal Rules of Evidence, Classes 1–19 (Fisher, Evidence, 4th ed.): jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy exclusions, character evidence and 404(b), impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, Bruton, the right to present a defense, and lay and expert opinion. Includes the outline, rule chart, flowcharts, flashcards, and bar-style practice questions.

subjects.title: Professional Responsibility
subjects.description: Model Rules of Professional Conduct and MPRE prep, Weeks 1–5 (Chs. 1–9, 20, 21): forming the client-lawyer relationship, competence, confidentiality, conflicts, and the duties that follow a representation from start to finish.

subjects.title: Con Law II
subjects.description: Constitutional Law II: the First Amendment, Chapters 1–6. Covers the Religion Clauses, the speech framework, incitement and national security, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech, including obscenity, child pornography, and indecency.

subjects.title: Sales and Leases
subjects.description: Sales and Leases of Goods under UCC Articles 1 and 2, Weeks 1–8 (Sepinuck, Chapters 1–6). Covers which law governs, formation and the battle of the forms, the statute of frauds, warranties and disclaimers, gap fillers, delivery and risk of loss, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment and delegation, repudiation, and excuse.

subjects.title: Agency & Partnership
subjects.description: Business Associations, Weeks 1–8 (Bainbridge, Park & Rodrigues, 6th ed.). Covers creating an agency, actual and apparent authority, ratification and estoppel, a principal's tort liability, agents' fiduciary duties, choosing an entity, partnership formation under the UPA and RUPA, partners' rights, authority and duties, dissociation and dissolution, loss sharing, buyout agreements, limited partnerships, and LLCs.

subjects.title: Contracts I
subjects.description: Contracts I, Weeks 1–9 (Epstein, Markell & Ponoroff, Making and Doing Deals, 7th ed.). Covers whether there is an enforceable agreement, the objective theory of assent, offers and their termination, options and firm offers, methods of acceptance and silence, the mirror-image rule and UCC § 2-207, misunderstanding, indefiniteness and letters of intent, consideration, modification, promissory estoppel, the statute of frauds, duress, and misrepresentation.

subjects.title: Civil Procedure
subjects.description: Civil Procedure, Weeks 1–9 (Spencer, Civil Procedure: A Contemporary Approach, 7th ed., and the Federal Civil Rules Supplement). Covers the court systems and sources of procedural law, personal jurisdiction from Pennoyer through Ford, notice and service of process under Rule 4, federal question, diversity, supplemental and removal jurisdiction, venue, transfer and forum non conveniens, the Erie doctrine through Shady Grove, pleading standards from Conley to Iqbal, Rule 11, and responding to the complaint under Rules 8, 12, and 55.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Evidence Outline
documents.description: Condensed exam outline of Classes 1–19 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Fisher pp. 1–783). Part I covers the Federal Rules, jury secrecy under 606(b), relevance, conditional relevance, and 403. Part II covers the specialized relevance rules, 407–411. Part III covers character evidence: the propensity ban, 404(b), Huddleston, 413–415, the defendant's and victim's character, and habit. Part IV covers impeachment under 607–609 and the rape shield. Part V covers competency, the definition of hearsay, opposing parties' statements, prior statements of witnesses, and the 803, 804, and 807 exceptions. Part VI covers the Confrontation Clause from Crawford through Smith v. Arizona. Part VII covers completeness, Bruton, and Chambers. Part VIII covers lay and expert opinion from the Week 10 reading. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every principal case with its class.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Federal Rules of Evidence
documents.description: The full official text of all 69 Federal Rules of Evidence, as amended to December 1, 2024. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 803(2) to go straight to the excited-utterance exception, or 404(b)(2) to see that clause marked), filter to the rules the course covers or to any of nine course topics, and follow cross-references between rules. Each rule shows how often the outline and the practice sets cite it. The practice sets use it for their Look up popup: any rule cited in a question or explanation opens its text with the cited subdivision marked.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Evidence Flowcharts
documents.description: Interactive decision charts for Weeks 1–5. Zoom and pan around each chart, walk through a rule one step at a time, and search all nine charts. Covers relevance (401–403), the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), impeachment, 609 convictions, the 412 rape shield, and 606(b) jury secrecy.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: FRE Rule Cards
documents.description: Flashcards for the Federal Rules of Evidence in Weeks 1–5. Pick your topics, flip each card, and rate yourself with a tap or a swipe. Missed cards come back sooner, and your mastery is saved in your browser.

documents.subject: evidence

documents.description: Conceptual multiple-choice questions for Weeks 1–5, weighted toward the Federal Rules. The answer order reshuffles every time you load the page, so you can't memorize the letters.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Evidence BAR style questions 1
documents.description: Bar-level application questions for Weeks 1–5. Each question sets two or three rules against each other and turns on a single fact. Every answer choice has its own explanation, and the set includes one-fact variations and a coverage map.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Evidence BAR style questions 2
documents.description: A second, all-new set of bar-style application questions covering Classes 1–10. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Includes one-fact variations and a coverage map of all 157 outline items.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Evidence Mock Midterm
documents.description: A timed practice exam for the night before the midterm: 60 new bar-style questions on Classes 1–10, in four 15-question parts that each cover every topic at the real exam’s 30-minute pace. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Evidence Mock Midterm II
documents.description: A second timed practice exam: 60 more new bar-style questions on Classes 1–10, with no fact patterns repeated from the first. It has the same four 15-question parts, each covering every topic at the real exam’s 30-minute pace, and draws on textbook problems the first exam didn’t use. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.

documents.subject: evidence
documents.title: Hearsay Practice Exam
documents.description: 40 bar-style questions, five choices each, covering all of hearsay: the definition and non-truth uses, opposing-party statements, prior statements and impeachment (613, 806), the 803 and 804 exceptions, 807, multiple hearsay, completeness under 106, and the Confrontation Clause through Smith v. Arizona and Samia. Includes the 2023 and 2024 amendments. Tutor mode grades each question as you go; timed mode gives you 80 minutes and grades at the end with a score by topic. Every question has the rule, an analysis, and why each choice is right or wrong.

documents.subject: professional-responsibility
documents.title: Pro Rep Drill
documents.description: 355 original MPRE-style application questions on Chs. 1–9, 20, 21 and the class slides. Use study mode for instant feedback or exam mode to be graded at the end. Filter by topic and shuffle the answer order.

documents.subject: professional-responsibility
documents.title: MPRE 500: Course Subset
documents.description: 298 of the 500 questions in Stevenson, 500 MPRE Practice Questions (2019), limited to what Weeks 1–5 cover. Uses the book's answer key, with study and exam modes, topic filters, and answer shuffling.

documents.subject: professional-responsibility
documents.title: Course Quiz
documents.description: The 54 multiple-choice questions from the class quizzes on Chs. 5, 6, 8, 20, and 21, checked against the course answer keys. Take the quiz for a score or open the answer view, with explanations drawn from Ethical Lawyering, the class slides, and the Model Rules.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Outline
documents.description: Case-by-case outline of Chapters 1–6, from Barnette and Kennedy v. Bremerton through Counterman, Ferber, and Free Speech Coalition v. Paxton. Each case has its rule, facts, holding, and dissent. Includes the Free Exercise, speech, prior restraint, and immoral speech checklists, along with synthesis tables.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Flowcharts
documents.description: Interactive decision charts for Chapters 1–6. A big-picture map shows how the Religion Clauses and the speech doctrines fit together, and eight charts walk through coercion, Free Exercise, the Establishment Clause and funding, the speech framework, incitement and fighting words, prior restraints, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech. Tap any box for a plain-English explanation, the cases behind it, and what to watch out for.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Quick Drill
documents.description: 264 multiple-choice questions on every case and concept in the outline. They test what each case held, hypotheticals built on its facts, and how the doctrine applies. Filter by chapter or question type, shuffle the answers, and review only the ones you missed.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment BAR style questions 1
documents.description: Bar-style application questions for Weeks 1–6 (Chapters 1–6). Each question sets out new facts, from compelled pledges and school prayer to protest livestreams, chatbot lawsuits, and age-verification laws, and asks you to apply the doctrine. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Includes one-fact variations and a coverage map of all 113 outline items.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Case Flash Cards
documents.description: 34 flashcards, one for each main case in Chapters 1–6, from Whitney and Barnette through Paxton and Brown. Each card asks what the case held, then gives the rule, the vote, and the key reasoning. Cited cases such as Gobitis, Yoder, Zelman, and Chaplinsky appear on the card for the case that cites them. Flip each card, then mark it Got it or Revisit.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Concept Flash Cards
documents.description: 32 flashcards on the core concepts of Chapters 1–6. Covers the Free Exercise and speech checklists, the ways a law fails neutrality, Establishment Clause funding, RFRA, the unprotected categories, overbreadth and vagueness, prior restraints, mens rea, the Miller test, and protecting kids versus adults.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Mock Exam
documents.description: A timed practice exam covering everything in Chapters 1–6: 60 bar-style questions with new facts, in four 15-question parts that each cover every topic at two minutes a question. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Case Repetition
documents.description: 349 quick questions for Chapters 1–6. 236 drill all 34 cases by their full names: name the case from its facts, its rule, or a key line, then recall its holding, its reasoning, and the cases it overruled or set up. 113 more drill the core concepts and elements across 23 topics, from strict scrutiny and the ways a law fails neutrality to the Brandenburg elements, Counterman’s recklessness standard, and the Miller prongs. Every question carries an illustration; when the picture would give the answer away, it stays blurred until you answer. Filter by chapter, question type, or a single case or topic.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Case Repetition, Volume 2
documents.description: 239 new questions on the same 34 cases and 23 topics as Volume 1, asked from different angles. Name each case from a new detail, then recall its holding, its reasoning, and the doctrine around it, plus 45 questions on core concepts and elements. 58 application questions put the rules to new fact patterns and explain why every wrong choice is wrong. Every question carries an illustration; when the picture would give the answer away, it stays blurred until you answer. Filter by chapter, question type, or a single case or topic.

documents.subject: con-law-ii
documents.title: First Amendment Essay Questions

Each essay sets out new facts with several questions, from a compelled state creed and a noise ordinance aimed at a night ceremony to a leaked convoy memo, threatening messages, and an AI companion app. Open the model answer for a full-credit response worked issue by issue, the cases it uses and why, the key concepts explained, and a 10-point scoring guide. Includes a case index and a coverage map of all 113 outline items.

documents.subject: sales-and-leases
documents.title: Sales and Leases Outline
documents.description: Condensed outline of Weeks 1–8 for the Week 10 assessment. 16 sections cover the UCC and governing law, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds and unconscionability, good faith and modification, express and implied warranties, quantity and price, delivery and risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, termination, insecurity and repudiation, and excuse, with worked problems. Case boxes mark main, note, and cited-only cases with their casebook pages and class slides.

documents.subject: sales-and-leases
documents.title: Sales and Leases Weighted Practice Exams
documents.description: Ten practice exams (150 new questions) for the Week 10 assessment, covering all of Weeks 1–8 with each topic's share set by how testable it is. Tier 1 gets 66 questions on the bright-line rules most likely to be tested: risk of loss and identification, implied warranties, express warranties, title and entrustment, and warranty disclaimers. Tier 2 gets 64: tender, inspection, acceptance and payment, course of performance and waiver, modification, quantity and price, the parol evidence rule, assignment and delegation, insecurity and repudiation, excuse, and remedy limits. Tier 3 gets 20: scope, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds, good faith and variation by agreement, and termination. Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format, mixing short hypos that ask who wins and why with "Which of the following is NOT…" questions. Wrong answers are built from the near-miss rules she tests, and some questions offer "None of the above," which is sometimes the answer. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or topic, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
headings: Sales and Leases Weighted Practice Exams

documents.subject: sales-and-leases
documents.title: Sales and Leases Acronym Exams
documents.description: Four practice exams (60 new questions) on just the acronyms: the shipping and delivery terms and the course shorthand. 40 questions cover §§ 2-319 to 2-324 and how each term moves the risk of loss: F.O.B. place of shipment and destination, F.O.B. vessel and F.A.S., C.I.F. and C. & F., ex-ship, "no arrival, no sale," C.O.D. and payment against documents, and what happens when there is no term or one side is in breach. The other 20 test the outline's shorthand: SOF, PER, NOM, CoP/CoD/UoT, LD, SOL, GFP and BIOCB, HTA and LOC (with PDM), DTW and CORS (Mathis), and UETA signatures. Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format, mixing short hypos that ask who bears the loss with "Which of the following is NOT…" questions. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or topic, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.

documents.subject: sales-and-leases
documents.title: Sales and Leases Complete Coverage Exams
documents.description: 31 quick-fire practice exams (465 new questions) that together test every rule and concept from Weeks 1–8. A checklist of 446 rules and concepts, built from every slide in the Week 1 through Week 8 decks, the Sepinuck casebook (cases, notes and assigned problems) and the statutory supplement (UCC text and Official Comments), was used to write them, and every item on it is tested at least once. The questions are short: one- or two-line rule questions and mini-hypos, many of them "Which of the following is NOT…" questions that test four or five rules at once. Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format and samples the whole course, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, repudiation and excuse. Wrong answers are the near misses: the common-law rule the UCC changed, the wrong number or section, merchant vs. non-merchant, the rule from the next section over. Some questions offer "None of the above" or "All of the above," and sometimes that is the answer. The 23 questions that change the facts of another question ("Same contract, but…") name the question they build on and show its facts, so shuffling or filtering never leaves you without them. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or by any of 24 topic areas, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
headings: Sales and Leases Complete Coverage Exams

Each exam samples the whole Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and together they cover all 16 sections: which law governs, formation and § 2-207, the statute of frauds, good faith and modification, express and implied warranties, title, quantity and price, delivery and acceptance, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, termination, insecurity and repudiation, and excuse. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.

documents.subject: sales-and-leases
documents.title: Sales and Leases Practice Exams II
documents.description: A second set of 14 practice exams (210 new questions) for the Week 10 assessment, in the same style as the first: Professor Richardson's sample-exam format, with 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions per exam that mix short hypos asking who wins and why with rule questions ("Which of the following is NOT…"), plus "None of the above" and "All of the above" choices that are sometimes the answer. Every fact pattern is new. The cases are tested by application, not recall: instead of asking what happened in Daitom, Casazza, Market Street, Roth Steel, Rogath, Razor, Top of Iowa, or the note cases, each question gives new facts that track the case (a pump buyer's purchase order that reserves its remedies, a lumber mill that threatens to stop shipping, a lamp buyer warned by an appraiser, an e-bike warranty sealed in the box, a farm that goes silent in an inverted market) and asks you to apply its rule. Each exam samples the whole Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, and together they cover all 16 sections and the assigned problems. Every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or outline section, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
headings: Sales and Leases Practice Exams II

documents.subject: sales-and-leases
documents.title: Sales and Leases Statutory Supplement
documents.description: Every UCC section the Weeks 1-8 outline and the practice sets cite (100 sections from Articles 1, 2, and 9), from Selected Commercial Statutes, 2026 edition, with the Official Comments. Section text is summarized in the statute's own key words and each comment is condensed; comments the outline or the practice questions rely on are marked. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 2-207 to go straight there), filter by any of the 16 outline sections, follow cross-references between sections, and open or close all the comments at once.

documents.subject: sales-and-leases
documents.title: Sales and Leases Focused Practice Exams
documents.description: Four practice exams (60 new questions) on just four topics: assignment and delegation (§ 2-210), liquidated damages (§ 2-718), warranties (§§ 2-312 to 2-318), and limited remedies (§ 2-719). Each exam has 15 stand-alone, five-choice questions in Professor Richardson's sample-exam format and covers all four topics, with warranties weighted most heavily: express and implied warranties, title and infringement, disclaimers, cumulation, and privity. Every fact pattern is new, cases are tested by application rather than recall, and every choice has its own explanation. Study mode checks each answer as you pick it; Exam mode lets you answer a full exam and then grade it. Filter by exam or topic, shuffle the questions, and retry the ones you missed.
headings: Sales and Leases Focused Practice Exams

documents.subject: sales-and-leases
documents.title: Sales and Leases Playlist
documents.description: Sixteen study songs that cover all 16 sections of the Weeks 1–8 condensed outline, from which law governs and the battle of the forms through warranties, risk of loss, disclaimers, remedies, the parol evidence rule, assignment, repudiation, and excuse. The main cases are sung through: Daitom, Casazza, Market Street, Roth Steel, Rogath, Orange & Rockland, Mathis, Razor, Santa Fe, Top of Iowa, and NIPSCO. It starts with track 1 and plays straight through; pick any track from the list, at 0.5×, 0.75×, normal, 1.25×, or 1.5× speed.

tracks.title: Is It Goods?
tracks.topic: Outline §1 · Scope and which law governs
tracks.description: The four factors that pick the governing law, what counts as goods under § 2-105 (and what does not: money, securities, things in action), things attached to land under § 2-107, and mixed deals of goods and services: the predominant-purpose test, the gravamen test from Anthony Pools, and the 2022 two-tier rule for hybrid transactions.

tracks.title: Battle of the Forms
tracks.description: A duet between buyer and seller. Formation under §§ 2-204 and 2-206, merchants' firm offers under § 2-205, and § 2-207: an acceptance with different terms still accepts unless it is expressly conditional, additional terms between merchants, and the knock-out rule. Case: Daitom v. Pennwalt, where the clashing limitation clauses dropped out and the four-year period of § 2-725 filled the gap.

tracks.title: You Never Signed It
tracks.topic: Outline §3 · Statute of frauds and unconscionability
tracks.description: The § 2-201 writing rule for sales of $500 or more (a record, signed by the party sued, stating a quantity), the four exceptions, and why promissory estoppel did not save the buyer in Casazza v. Kiser. Then § 2-302 unconscionability: procedural and substantive, decided by the court as of the time the deal was made.

tracks.title: Good Faith
tracks.topic: Outline §4 · Good faith and course of performance
tracks.description: The § 1-304 duty of good faith (honesty in fact plus fair dealing), which cannot be disclaimed and is not a claim of its own. Market Street Associates v. Frey on exploiting the other side's oversight, with Brunswick Hills and Vintage Rodeo, and the § 1-303 hierarchy: express terms, course of performance, course of dealing, usage of trade.

tracks.title: Pay More or Get Nothing
tracks.description: Section 2-209: modifications need no consideration but must be in good faith, and Roth Steel v. Sharon Steel holds that a price increase extracted by threatening to stop performing is not. No-oral-modification clauses, the statute of frauds applied to the deal as modified, waiver and its retraction, and estoppel.

tracks.title: Promise or Puff?
tracks.description: The three ways to make an express warranty under § 2-313 (affirmation of fact, description, sample or model), the basis-of-the-bargain test without proof of reliance, and the line between specific facts and puffing. Case: Rogath v. Siebenmann, the Francis Bacon painting, on whether a buyer who learns of doubts still keeps the warranty.

tracks.title: Implied
tracks.description: Merchantability under § 2-314 and its six standards, fitness for a particular purpose under § 2-315 (with the Ingram River barges), and the warranty of title and against infringement under § 2-312. Also voidable title and entrustment under § 2-403, and the three privity alternatives of § 2-318.

tracks.title: Fill in the Blanks
tracks.topic: Outline §6–7 · Gap fillers, quantity and price
tracks.description: Open terms under § 2-204(3) and the delivery, time, and payment gap fillers. Output and requirements contracts under § 2-306 (good faith and no unreasonably disproportionate quantity, from Orange & Rockland v. Amerada Hess), and open price under § 2-305, including a price set by one party in bad faith in Mathis v. Exxon and the majority view that rejects it.

tracks.title: Accept or Reject
tracks.description: Tender and payment as concurrent conditions, the seller's tender under § 2-503, the buyer's right to inspect under § 2-513, acceptance under § 2-606, perfect tender and installment contracts, cure under § 2-508, the buyer's duties after rejecting, and revocation of acceptance under § 2-608.

tracks.title: Risk of Loss
tracks.description: A call-and-response duet on who bears the loss when goods are destroyed. The agreement first, then the breaching party under § 2-510, then § 2-509: shipment and destination contracts, goods held by a bailee, and everything else (merchant sellers on receipt, non-merchants on tender). Also F.O.B. and C.I.F. terms and the seller's shipping duties under § 2-504.

tracks.title: Make It Conspicuous
tracks.topic: Outline §10 · Variation by agreement and disclaimers
tracks.description: What § 1-302 lets the parties change and what it does not, and disclaimers under § 2-316: mention merchantability, put fitness in a conspicuous writing, "as is" and "with all faults," examination of the goods, and trade usage. Why express warranties are nearly impossible to disclaim, and why title needs specific language.

tracks.title: Two Walls
tracks.description: The buyer's and seller's damage formulas, incidental and consequential damages under § 2-715, liquidated damages under § 2-718, and limited remedies under § 2-719. Case: Razor v. Hyundai, where the repair remedy failed of its essential purpose but the exclusion of consequential damages stood or fell on its own, as unconscionable.

tracks.title: Parol Evidence Rule
tracks.description: Section 2-202: a final writing cannot be contradicted by prior or contemporaneous agreements but can be explained or supplemented, and a complete and exclusive one cannot be supplemented either. What the rule never bars (later modifications, fraud, conditions precedent), how merger clauses work, and how it interacts with § 2-316(1) when oral warranties meet an "as is" writing.

tracks.title: Passing It On
tracks.description: Assigning rights and delegating duties under § 2-210, anti-assignment clauses and § 9-406(d), and the difference between cancellation and termination under § 2-106. Then ending an indefinite contract on reasonable notice under § 2-309, with Santa Fe Custom Shutters v. Home Depot: no lost profits for ending an at-will deal.

tracks.title: Adequate Assurance
tracks.description: A duet between an anxious party and a reassuring one. Demanding adequate assurance under § 2-609 and the 30-day limit, anticipatory repudiation under § 2-610, and retraction under § 2-611. Cases: Top of Iowa Coop v. Sime Farms on hedge-to-arrive corn contracts, and PDM v. Brookhaven on demanding more than is adequate.

tracks.title: Excuse
tracks.description: The closing anthem. Casualty to identified goods under § 2-613, substituted performance under § 2-614, impracticability and fair allocation under §§ 2-615 and 2-616, and frustration of purpose at common law. Case: NIPSCO v. Carbon County Coal, where a buyer that misjudged the market could not walk away from a fixed-price contract.

tracks.title: Power to Leave
tracks.description: At-will versus term partnerships, and a partner's power to leave versus the right to. UPA automatic dissolution against the RUPA § 603 buyout path, and judicial expulsion. Cases: Collins v. Lewis, Giles, and Page v. Page.

tracks.title: Winding Up
tracks.topic: Outline §10 · Liquidation, buyouts and lingering authority
tracks.description: Statements of dissociation that cut off lingering liability after 90 days, § 701 buyouts at the greater of liquidation or going-concern value, and no forced fire sale. Cases: Creel v. Lilly, Monin v. Monin, and Pav-Saver.

tracks.title: Money vs. Sweat
tracks.topic: Outline §11–12 · Loss sharing and buyout agreements
tracks.description: The Kovacik v. Reed exception, where the money partner bears the cash losses and the service partner loses only their labor, why RUPA rejects it, and the traps in buyout agreements (G & S Investments v. Belman).

tracks.title: Welcome to the Fortress
tracks.topic: Outline §13–14 · LPs, LLCs and veil piercing
tracks.description: General partners' unlimited liability against the LP, LLP and LLC shields; the corporate general partner in Frigidaire v. Union Properties; LLCs as creatures of contract under the ULLCA, member-managed and manager-managed; and veil piercing as the only way through the shield.
